nodes.label: ErrorCode registry in error_codes.rs
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L03699] The 18 already-declared UPDATER_/DISTRIBUTION_/AUTOSTART_ constants are the only codes this chunk may use; error_codes.rs is owned by another chunk and no code may be added. Each carries an `english` field used as the String payload, verified declared=1 for all 18 at L6069.
nodes.summary: Reused id. Same claim as chunk-084: a central const registry whose `english` field is the canonical user-facing fallback, referenced as `CODE.english.to_string()` inside `Err(...)`. This chunk is a pure consumer of it — 18 codes across updater_cmds.rs, distribution.rs, autostart.rs and autostart/store_startup.rs, every one verified present by grepping `^pub const <CODE>:` in error_codes.rs.

nodes.label: include_str! retired-literal guard
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L6040] Two first drafts were discarded. (a) A RETIRED_RAW_MESSAGES list inside the file it guards made the guard self-referential — it always failed, because include_str! reads the whole file including the test module. (b) A whitespace-normalised `Err( "` shape guard never matched, because normalization does not insert a space. The final guard reads `code.english` from the registry, so the test file cannot reintroduce the prose it checks for. Paths are macro-relative (`"updater_cmds.rs"`, not `"commands/…"`).
nodes.summary: Reused id. Same mechanism as chunk-084 — an include_str! assertion in the guarded file's own test module that fails if the retired prose is re-inlined — but this chunk arrives at the non-self-referential form independently and by discarding two working-looking drafts first. Coverage caveat recorded at L6092: the guard matches the canonical `english` text, so the two sites whose old prose differed by design (`:301` dropped a `{version}` echo, `autostart.rs:46` dropped `{e}`) are guarded by review only.

nodes.label: Zero-subagent-compiler policy
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L38] The host is memory-constrained and interactive; local compilation risks a hard reset. So verification was source reading, grep, sed -n, awk and git show only, and every cargo invocation was handed to the parent over ssh on vps-bcb with --lib and -j 4. Confirmed in the report at L6030: no cargo, rustc, clippy, nextest, rustfmt or mold was run, locally or via script.
nodes.summary: Reused id, sixth existing owner. Same claim. Here the policy is stated as the chunk's first hard rule and compliance is an explicit line in the report, which is what the contract's rationale field is for.

nodes.label: Shrink-only budget ratchet
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L6100] rustRawErrorBudget in completenessNewBudgets.ts is asserted with toEqual, exact. Emptying three entries therefore breaks the test until they are deleted: "commands/updater_cmds.rs": 2, "distribution.rs": 2, "autostart/store_startup.rs": 5. autostart.rs has no entry because its site used AutoStartError(format!(…)), which the \bErr\(\s*" regex never counted.
nodes.summary: Reused id, third existing owner (chunk-087, chunk-rem-079). Same claim. The mechanism is quoted verbatim from the scanner's own doc comment at L2444: a file with no hit is omitted rather than recorded as zero, so cleaning a file makes its ledger entry stale and the exact-equality assertion fails until the entry is removed.

nodes.label: An unmapped HTTP status takes the existing catch-all code and the status goes to a log
nodes.norm_label: unmapped http status takes the existing catch-all code and the status goes to a log
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L06078] friendly_rollback_status_message at :312 interpolated an HTTP status for which no code existed, and error_codes.rs was not this chunk's to edit. UPDATER_ROLLBACK_LIST_FAILED is the existing catch-all and 5xx already claims LIST_UNAVAILABLE, so an unmapped status is exactly "the list failed to load". The user learns the same thing and gets the same retry advice; the status is no longer echoed, which was the point of the migration. No code added. New test friendly_rollback_error_does_not_echo_an_unmapped_status covers 400/401/418/501.
nodes.summary: The interpolation that is dropped is the OS/HTTP detail, not the diagnosis — it moves to log::warn!("[UPDATER] rollback list returned unexpected HTTP {status}.") while the user-facing String becomes UPDATER_ROLLBACK_LIST_FAILED.english. The prompt at L71 offered two options, add nothing and report debt or map to the catch-all; the note chose the second and justified it rather than deferring.

nodes.label: Cfg-gate an import to match the items that use it
nodes.norm_label: cfg gate an import to match its only users
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L6092] CI runs cargo clippy -- -D warnings with no --tests, so test code is not linted and an ungated import used only by a cfg(test) module escapes. But store_startup.rs is entirely cfg(any(windows, test)) and autostart.rs's only user is cfg(not(all(windows, feature="microsoft-store"))), so on a non-Windows or Store build those imports are genuinely dead and would fail the lint.
nodes.summary: Both imports were re-gated to the exact union of their users: #[cfg(any(windows, test))] in store_startup.rs, and #[cfg(any(not(all(windows, feature = "microsoft-store")), test))] in autostart.rs. Derived in the working at L5417-L5435 by enumerating the four build configurations rather than guessing: on non-test Linux every item in store_startup.rs is cfg'd out, so every error_codes import there is unused.

nodes.label: Keep Result<_, String> signatures until the callers move to a structured error
nodes.norm_label: keep result string signatures until the callers move to a structured error
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - c9d-updater-autostart-errors [ses_f20b36cf2ffeuIbTv7dPiZyrYs].md:L6069] ensure_direct_updates()? is propagated with ? by three #[tauri::command]s, and autostart's Box<dyn StdError> is propagated by setup/init.rs:157 and control_api/routes.rs:233. Signature changes are out of this chunk's scope and would break those callers.
nodes.summary: Replacing the prose with codes does not require changing what the functions return. The file doc comment records the intended endpoint: once the commands::updater_cmds callers move to AppErrorResponse, each site becomes a static_err call with no other change.

nodes.label: OpenCode v2 plugin contract breaks V1-era plugins
nodes.norm_label: opencode v2 plugin contract breaks v1-era plugins
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - fixing-rtk-ts-plugin-export-error [ses_f07e59934ffe54cIUVGVCRxjxw].md:L6495] V2 requires a default export with id + setup, hooks registered via ctx.tool.hook("execute.before") / ctx.shell.hook("create.before"), and node:child_process instead of the Bun $ helper. The V1 form — import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin" plus export const RtkOpenCodePlugin returning a "tool.execute.before" map — is rejected with err_7e3d8681, "Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or setup function".
nodes.summary: Reused id, second existing owner (chunk-rem-024, which found the same rtk 0.50.0 plugin still on the V1 API and worked around it via MCP instead). Here the V1 form is migrated rather than routed around. Read at L5562-L5566 of the note: the @opencode/plugin 2.0.21 type surface is exactly `interface Plugin { readonly id: string; readonly setup: (context: Context) => ... }` with `export declare function define(plugin: Plugin): Plugin`.

nodes.label: A bare plugin file has no node_modules, so a runtime import from @opencode/plugin cannot resolve
nodes.norm_label: a bare plugin file has no node modules for a runtime import
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - fixing-rtk-ts-plugin-export-error [ses_f07e59934ffe54cIUVGVCRxjxw].md:L9916] A file under ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ is loaded as-is with no node_modules above it, so `import { Plugin } from "@opencode/plugin"` dies at load with ResolveMessage: Cannot find package '@opencode/plugin' — err_abe16872 and err_a00ff8a6 in the server log — and no hook ever fires, with no error visible to the user. `import type` is erased at transpile time and never resolved, so it is safe; the default export is then a plain object with id + setup, which is all V2 requires. node:child_process is a builtin specifier and always resolves. The same pattern as ~/ai-skills/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js, which the log shows loading successfully at L8579 while rtk.ts failed.
nodes.summary: Third of three sequential bugs, and the one that produced no user-visible error at all — `opencode plugin list` showed the plugin loaded with no failure status while not a single hook fired. Distinguished from the V1/V2 contract break by its symptom: err_7e3d8681 names the missing default export, this failure is silent from the CLI's point of view and only appears as a WARN in ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log.

nodes.label: rtk rewrite 0.50.0 exits 3 on success, so decide from stdout rather than the exit code
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - fixing-rtk-ts-plugin-export-error [ses_f07e59934ffe54cIUVGVCRxjxw].md:L9915] Measured directly, not inferred from the help text: `rtk rewrite --help` says "Exits 0 and prints the rewritten command if supported. Exits 1 with no output if the command has no RTK equivalent", but 0.50.0 actually exits 3 with stdout filled on success and exits 1 with empty stdout when there is no equivalent. Confirmed across `git status`, `ls -la`, `git log --oneline -5`, `cat hello.txt` and `cargo test`, all exit=3 (L6844-L6847), and `echo hello` exit=1 with empty stdout (L6760). The fix drops the exit-code branch entirely and keeps the stdout comparison.
nodes.summary: Second of three sequential bugs, and the one with no error message either: the plugin loaded, the hook fired, and the rewrite silently never applied, because `if (result.status !== 0) return undefined` discarded every successful rewrite. The three-way measurement is at L6890-L6892 — an already-rewritten `rtk git status` also exits 3 with stdout equal to the input, so the guard also needs the rewritten !== command check to avoid a no-op rewrite.

nodes.label: Prove a rewrite hook fired from the spawn line the server writes
nodes.norm_label: prove a rewrite hook fired from the spawn line in the server log
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-10-01 - fixing-rtk-ts-plugin-export-error [ses_f07e59934ffe54cIUVGVCRxjxw].md:L9905] `opencode plugin list` showed the plugin loaded and `bun build` bundled the file clean while not one hook had fired, so neither was evidence. The e2e test asks an agent to run `git status` in a staged temp git repo and then reads the server log, where the agent's request appears as command=/usr/bin/bash args="[\"-c\",\"rtk git status\"]" — the agent asked for `git status`, and what executed was `rtk git status`.
nodes.summary: The log line is the only artefact that distinguishes 'the hook fired and rewrote' from 'the hook fired and passed through unchanged', which is exactly the failure mode of the exit-3 bug. This is the positive control the session lacked for its first two verification passes; the same technique as the parecord capture in the machine's own AGENTS.md, where the mixer shows Volume 100% over digital silence.
